newsitem.title: USA: Trump Hotel seen mulling Hard Rock theme at Castle.
newsitem.headline: Trump Hotel seen mulling Hard Rock theme at Castle.

text.p: Trump Castle is expected to be soon turned over to Trump Hotels & Casino Resorts Inc, which is already exploring how to turn the Atlantic City casino into a Hard Rock Cafe-themed gaming complex.

Sources familiar with the situation said Trump Hotels shareholders are expected to approve the $500 million acquisition of the Castle from Donald Trump at a special shareholder meeting set for Monday in New York City.

They also said Trump Hotels is expected then to initiate discussions with London-based Rank Organisation Plc about renovating the Castle into a casino resort sporting the successful, youth-oriented Hard Rock Cafe theme.

With the approval, Trump would be a three-casino juggernaut in Atlantic City under pressure to draw new players to a market with stunted revenue growth relative to Las Vegas and major operators suffering from crimped earnings and declining margins because of intense competition.
"We are confident, based on conversations with institutional shareholders, that the acquisition will be approved," said a source familiar with the situation.
Trump Hotels agreed three months ago to exchange 5.837 million common shares and $884,500 in cash for the Castle and assume $348 million in outstanding Castle obligations and debt.
With the shareholder approval, the Castle would become part of Trump's gaming empire composed of the Taj Mahal, Trump Plaza and a riverboat casino near Gary, Indiana.

As for Hard Rock, sources close to Trump said "re-theming" of the Castle is a top priority and a deal with Rank could lead to the same spectacular success of the Hard Rock Cafe & Casino in Las Vegas, opened last year.
Rank is a likely partner because the two companies already are familiar with each other from the installation of a Hard Rock Cafe at the Trump Taj Mahal.

Such an alliance also makes sense as a competitive response to ITT Corp's agreement with Planet Hollywood to develop themed hotel/casinos in Atlantic City, Las Vegas and other resort areas, analysts said.

"They are exploring alternatives to re-theme the Castle and among those being considered is the Hard Rock, a Trump's marina with a modern nautical theme, or other concept that appeals to a new, younger demographic," one of the sources said.
"The Hard Rock (Las Vegas) is a huge success. It expanded the market there dramatically and jump-started the 25 to 30 group and Atlantic City is screaming, screaming for a new concept," he said.
The nautical theme has already been exploited by Harrah's Entertainment Inc's Atlantic City operation.

"They have a Hard Rock in the Taj, so Trump knows the concept well and they have a great relationship with Rank. It's an idea at this stage and they have been waiting for the (shareholder) vote to proceed," the source said.
A Trump spokeswoman declined to comment and a spokesman for the Hard Rock's U.S. operations based in Orlando, Fla. said "there is no foundation" to the Castle speculation.

In June, Rank paid Hard Rock founder Peter Morton $410 million for the chain founded 25 years ago in London, a deal that added 13 Hard Rock Cafes and four franchises to the 15 cafes and 26 franchises Rank already owned.
Rank then said it intended to open another seven cafes within 12 month, one of them being a Hard Rock Cafe due to open in the Taj Mahal in November.
